items.title: David Murray interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 18, 2003
items.q: we believed in Martin Luther King, and that was the same year that Martin Luther King was killed.

ctx.x: How did your father feel about your being involved in those kinds of things, even though it wasn’t a conscious choice, as you said, the circumstance kind of put you into it and you reacted.

Well my father is from the school of — civil rights was very high on his list. Even being a staunch church man, we believed in Martin Luther King, and that was the same year that Martin Luther King was killed. So my father was for anything that had anything to do with making the situation better. I mean the fact that he moved to Berkeley and put us in a better neighborhood than our cousins who lived in Oakland — I remember one of the most angry times that I’ve ever seen him was when my brother moved into a ghetto…
